title: Why Is the Labor Market Stuck?
partialText: Our chief economics correspondent, Ben Casselman, describes how a “low-hire, low-fire” labor market has left American job-seekers in a bind.

title: What to know about the report.
Parents Who Borrowed for Children’s College Face Looming Deadline
partialText: New rules mean that parent PLUS loans have to be consolidated into a new loan by June 30 for parents to keep affordable payments. But the deadline is really earlier to allow time for processing.

title: Trump Requests $1.5 Trillion for Military Spending
partialText: The huge proposed increase would be partly offset by steep cuts to domestic programs, some of which the Trump administration describes as wasteful.

title: Strong Jobs Numbers Make the Fed’s Job Easier
partialText: Robust job growth in March suggests that the labor market remains relatively healthy, allowing officials at the central bank to focus on fighting inflation.

title: The White House is readying a budget for the statistics agency that compiles the jobs report.
partialText: President Trump is set to release his new spending plan on Friday, after trying last year to cut funding for the federal bureau tasked with measuring the economy.

title: What to know about the report.
Economists Are Drawing Stronger Connections Between A.I. and Jobs
partialText: Artificial intelligence hasn’t disrupted the labor market, economists say, but they are increasingly convinced that it will — and that policymakers are unprepared.

title: Skilled Foreign Workers Think About Leaving the U.S.
partialText: As the Trump administration cracks down on the H-1B visa program, which allows skilled workers like software engineers to work in the United States, foreign professionals are debating whether to stay and build careers or quit the American Dream.

title: Jobs and Workers Are In Balance. Nobody Is Happy About It.
partialText: Lower immigration has brought labor supply in line with shaky demand, but economists worry that such a slow-moving job market is at risk of toppling over.

title: How New Yorkers Spend, Splurge and Scrimp to Live in the City
partialText: Eliza Shapiro, who reports on New York City’s affordability crisis, asked hundreds of residents to get candid about their finances.

title: Rival Nations Seize On Choke Points to Counter Trump
partialText: From Iran to China, President Trump’s global aggression has encouraged other countries to search for new ways to pressure the U.S. economy.

title: JetBlue Raises Checked Bag Fees as Fuel Costs Soar
partialText: The airline, which now charges up to $59 for one checked bag on a domestic flight, could influence other carriers strained by the war in Iran.

title: Hershey’s Promises to Use Only Real Chocolate After Backlash
partialText: The change follows weeks of complaints from a grandson of the Reese’s Peanut Butter Cup inventor and other vocal consumers.

title: Trump Revamps Metal and Pharmaceutical Tariffs
partialText: The administration announced new levies and made changes to existing tariffs for industries that have proved influential on the president’s trade policy.

title: Republicans Seek Protections for Oil Giants Against Climate Lawsuits
partialText: Utah passed a law to insulate oil companies against efforts to make them pay for their role in global warming. A nationwide version is in the works.

title: War With Iran Clarifies Trump’s Spending Priorities: The Military, Not Child Care
partialText: As the White House prepares to release its 2027 budget, President Trump said military protection, not social programs, took precedence.

title: Blue Owl, Ailing Private Credit Firm, Reveals Even More Troubles
partialText: Investors in the struggling Wall Street lender put in record requests to get their money back.

title: Mortgage Rates Climb for 5th Week as Iran War Weighs on U.S. Housing Market
partialText: The average rate on a 30-year mortgage in the United States jumped to 6.46 percent, making it harder for buyers to afford homes.

title: Trump’s Media-Bashing Is Coming Back to Bite Him in Court
partialText: Judges have cited attacks on the press by the president and his appointees when ruling against the government in at least three court cases.

title: Trump Faces a Tough Fight With His New Budget
partialText: Last year, the president proposed many steep spending cuts that Congress never granted. This time, he may face an even tougher sell.

title: Investigators Said to Look at Whether LaGuardia Controller Stepped Away
partialText: Officials are said to be examining whether a controller had to use an emergency phone just before the crash at LaGuardia. They have yet to determine the cause of the crash and are also focusing on other avenues.

title: What the Iran War Could Mean for Stocks, Bonds and Growth
partialText: A merely bad outlook might be good enough for the markets, our columnist says.

title: Tesla Sales Rise as $4-a-Gallon Gas Revives Interest in E.V.s
partialText: The repeal of tax credits last year sent electric vehicle sales plummeting. But with gas prices soaring, consumers are taking another, cautious, look.

title: Why Stocks Tumbled After Trump’s Iran Address
partialText: Oil surged and stocks sold off after the president delivered an unclear case for continuing the war in the Middle East.

title: Europe Pushes for a Gentler Internet for Children
partialText: The European Union and national capitals are trying to make social media and algorithms less addictive and safer, especially for children.

title: The Revival of the Fashion-Tech Love Affair
partialText: Get ready for the return of wearables and a new stage in the fashion-tech relationship.

title: How A.I. Helped One Man (and His Brother) Build a $1.8 Billion Company
partialText: Who needs more than two employees when artificial intelligence can do so many corporate tasks? It’s super efficient — and a little bit lonely.

title: Six Flags Was a Summer Destination. Can It Win Families Back?
partialText: There has never been more competition in the leisure industry, as Disney and niche parks appeal to young families and high-income visitors.

title: Iran War Showcases Strength of South Korean Defense Sector
partialText: Missile interceptors made by the South Korean firm LIG Nex1 are said to be performing well, at a small fraction of the cost of U.S. interceptors.

title: Oil Stocks and Gas Prices Swing After Trump’s Speech on Iran
partialText: President Trump’s statements about continuing to strike Iran spooked investors, though markets recovered after reports that Oman and Iran were in talks to monitor Strait of Hormuz traffic.

title: U.S. Lifts Sanctions on Venezuela’s New Leader, Delcy Rodríguez
partialText: Removing sanctions would allow Delcy Rodríguez, the country’s acting leader, to conduct business with U.S. companies and potentially meet with President Trump.

title: Goodbye ‘Geeky Hunk’? Gmail Users Can Now Change Their Usernames.
partialText: Users who have been saddled with now-cringe email handles since the mid-2000s can now change them without losing any data under a policy Google announced on Wednesday.

title: Trump Officials Try to Fight Foreign Disinformation They Once Dismissed
partialText: The war in Iran has exposed the need to mount a defense against foreign influence campaigns, officials and experts say.

title: G.M. Reports Sharp Decline in Car Sales Amid War and High Prices
partialText: Toyota, Honda and Hyundai reported drops in March. Some blamed gasoline prices.

title: Elon Musk’s SpaceX Files to Go Public, Setting Stage for Huge I.P.O.
partialText: An initial public offering of Elon Musk’s rocket and satellite company would most likely be a generational wealth event and one of the largest offerings ever.

title: Markets Bet Big on a Quick End to the Iran War
partialText: Global markets rallied as President Trump signaled that the United States may stop fighting soon. But big questions remain about lingering damage.

title: Robot Taxis Stop in Traffic in Chinese City, Stranding Travelers
partialText: The authorities in Wuhan, the site of one of the world’s largest experiments in self-driving cars, cited a “system failure” after widespread reports on Tuesday evening.

title: Markets Extend Rally and Oil Prices Drop After Trump Says Iran War Will Wind Down
partialText: President Trump said the U.S. military would wrap up its campaign in Iran in two or three weeks.

title: Judge Dismisses Lawsuit That Challenged Ban on Endorsements by Churches
partialText: Conservatives had expected a victory in the case after the I.R.S. agreed to a settlement that allowed churches to voice support for candidates.

title: Justice Dept. Struggles to Respond to Trump’s Suit Against IRS
partialText: Officials at the department and the White House are in the middle of a messy and complicated debate over how to respond to President Trump’s lawsuit demanding $10 billion from the I.R.S.

title: Judge Blocks Trump’s Order to End Funding for NPR and PBS
partialText: The ruling will have minimal effect on the federal money going to public media because Congress voted to claw back funding. But it could have implications for any future funding.

title: Allbirds, Once Silicon Valley’s Favorite Shoe, Sells for $39 Million
partialText: Despite once being valued at $4 billion, the company that made sneakers from Merino wool struggled to capture a wide customer base and turn a profit.

title: March Madness Puts Las Vegas Back in the Game
partialText: The influx of fans during this month’s college basketball tournament is a welcome lift to the city’s casinos and hotels after a dismal 2025, when the number of visitors fell 7.5 percent.

title: Global Ban on Digital Duties Expires After Stalled Talks at W.T.O.
partialText: A prohibition on taxing digital downloads expired, after members of the World Trade Organization concluded their annual meeting without an agreement.

title: Eli Lilly Will Buy a Narcolepsy Drug Developer for $6.3 Billion
partialText: Eli Lilly plans to acquire Centessa Pharmaceuticals, which has been conducting a midstage clinical trial of its lead drug.

title: McCormick to Combine With Unilever Food Unit to Create a Spice Giant
partialText: The deal ends Unilever’s time in the food industry and will create a multibillion-dollar group under the McCormick name.

title: FDA Is Expected to Lift Restriction on Peptides, Heeding RFK Jr.’s Wishes
partialText: The peptides, which are increasingly marketed as providing longevity and health benefits, were removed in 2023 from the agency’s list of products that compounding pharmacies can sell.
